abstract: The biogenic amine 5-hydroxytryptamine (serotonin, 5-HT) regulates social behavior across the animal kingdom. Although drugs that promote 5-HT transporter (SERT)-mediated 5-HT efflux within the nucleus accumbens (NAc) enhance sociability, the extent to which endogenous mechanisms regulating SERT contribute to normal social behavior is unknown. Prior in vitro studies have shown that SERT trafficking and activity are controlled by transporter phosphorylation, with the Thr276 site required for rapid, protein kinase G (PKG)-dependent increases in SERT function. Using SERT Ala276 knock-in mice, we demonstrate that sex-specific social behaviors rely on the capacity to phosphorylate SERT at Thr276. Whereas WT males and females exhibited social preference and sustained interactions with juvenile mice, these behaviors were selectively diminished in Ala276 females. In contrast, Ala276 males exhibited preserved sociability but increased retreat behavior in the tube dominance test. Dorsal and ventral brain slice biotinylation studies revealed sex-independent, PKG-induced increases in striatal SERT surface expression that were abolished in Ala276 mice. In the dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN), PKG activation failed to elevate SERT surface expression in either sex. Extracellular 5-HT responses in the NAc recorded via in vivo fiber photometry during repeated, but not initial, social interactions were absent in Ala276 females but not males. Ex vivo patch clamp recordings from DRN slices uncovered reduced excitability of 5-HT neurons from female Ala276 mice compared with WT controls, an effect reversed by blockade of 5-HT1A autoreceptors, consistent with tonic activation of these receptors in mutants. Supporting this idea, systemic administration of the 5-HT1A partial agonist buspirone restored sociability in Ala276 females and social dominance in Ala276 males, while elevating extracellular NAc 5-HT responses in Ala276 females. Our findings support a model in which sustained social behavior requires the capacity to phosphorylate SERT at Thr276 to limit somatodendritic 5-HT1A autoreceptor-mediated inhibition and support serotonergic signaling.
